title: modal and nonmodal dialogs
rule: Modal & Nonmodal Dialogs (7 numbered): (1) Important warnings / prevent or correct critical errors. (2) Request info critical to continuing the current process. (3) May fragment a complex workflow into simpler steps. (4) Ask for info that, if provided, significantly lessens work. (5) Do not use for nonessential, off-flow information. (6) Avoid interrupting high-stake processes such as checkout. (7) Avoid when the decision needs sources unavailable inside the modal.
pass_when: A modal is used for 1–4; not used for 5–7 (nonessential off-flow; interrupting checkout; decision needs outside sources).
fail_when: Modal for nonessential/off-flow; modal interrupting checkout; modal that needs sources not inside it; or no modal when a critical warning / critical-to-continue request applies.
overview: A modal is only for a required finish-or-cancel; other layers stay nonmodal.
apply_when: Choosing modal vs accordion, tooltip, or side panel.
not_when: The destructive decision inside a dialog — that is protect_destructive_and_leave.
agent_hint: Pick the layer for the content. Do not treat every dialog as modal.
description: Use a modal only when the user must finish or cancel before continuing. The overlay type should match whether they may keep working in the background. A modal that blocks the page for content that is not a required decision fails. This is about the layer, not the destructive copy inside it.
do_not_claim: Confirmation-dialog copy (`actions.confirm.*`); form-error-only-in-modal (`forms.errors.modal_not_only_copy`); Polar complex-form modal (dual-cite, keep both named).
